The accepted locality threshold is met because e/d≤1/(64d³). Every minimizing facet centroid is an actual A_e point within 8d²e≤1/(8d²) of the matching old centroid. The nonmatched barycentric coordinates stay at least 7/(8d), and the coordinate sum is at least (d−1)/d−1/(8d)≥7/16>e.

The actual matched centroid belongs to the boundary of A_e, and all defining constraints except the matching old facet are strict there. Its unique support plane must therefore be the corresponding old facet plane. This identifies every facet of every minimizing simplex with T.

The interval [ae,a]∩[s−bt,s] is nonempty when ae≤s≤a+bt. The decomposition along the point's own ray proves the exact weighted Minkowski region, and subtraction of the homothetic inner simplex gives the displayed volume polynomial.

After dividing A_e+B by 1+t the truncation parameter becomes e/(1+t), still admissible. The exact defect polynomial has only the pure a^d term; both unit weights are positive and attain equality. Scaling to half weights leaves the equality unchanged.

dependencies.hypotheses: Apply at dimension d to the full-dimensional A_e, with infinity-norm Hausdorff distance δ=e/d≤1/(64d³). The minimum enclosures and matched facet centroids meet the precise distance and actual contact hypotheses.

Apply the revised theorem’s unchanged first clause to the two positive full-dimensional compact convex summands A_e and B=tT with weights one. Their sum K is {x≥0, e≤∑x≤1+t}. Its enclosing simplex S=(1+t)T supports K on every facet: d≥2 allows the minimum of each coordinate to be attained at zero in another coordinate direction, and the coordinate sum attains 1+t. The parallel summand enclosures in those same normals are T and tT by their actual coordinate minima and coordinate-sum maxima. The added Q assumption belongs to the separate containing-body clause and is unnecessary for this invocation. The exact weighted volume polynomial removes only (ae)^d|T|, so the equality example and all cross-defect conclusions are unchanged.
